//: Cursor's project hook wiring. The Claude Code equivalent is .claude/settings.json; both point at the SAME scripts in .claude/hooks/, which are host-agnostic since _lib.mjs normalises the payload and output shapes. Two copies of a guard, one per editor, is how one of them silently stops being enforced.
//scripts-location: The scripts still live under .claude/hooks/ even though they are no longer Claude-only. Renaming that folder means touching settings.json, build-plugin.mjs, every doc and the generated plugin tree - and then moving them a second time when the core/ + adapters/ split happens. It is deliberately left for that change.
//matchers: Deliberately absent on preToolUse. A matcher that does not match is a guard that silently never fires, and the scripts already exit 0 in microseconds when the payload is not theirs. Fail-safe beats fail-silent for a security guard.
//failClosed: Cursor's default when a hook crashes, times out or returns malformed output is to let the tool call proceed. For a guard that is the wrong default: a node that is not on PATH, a syntax error from a bad merge, or a payload the script did not expect would each turn every guard off with nothing on screen. failClosed:true on the four guards makes those cases a denial the user can see. Two consequences: Cursor counts 'exit 0, no stdout' as a failure too, so _lib.ok() answers {permission:"allow"} explicitly on the deciding events (self-audit A10 checks that line is still there); and the advisory hooks (sessionStart, afterFileEdit, stop) stay fail-open, because blocking work over a digest that could not be built would be the opposite mistake.

beforeShellExecution.//: Cursor's purpose-built shell hook. Better than routing shell through preToolUse: it fires only for commands, carries the command at the top level, and can answer 'ask' as well as 'deny'.

beforeMCPExecution.//: The database and the GitHub account are reachable through MCP, and until now nothing in this repo had an opinion about that. Policy lives in .cursor/mcp-policy.json.

beforeReadFile.//: The same refusal Claude Code has always had in .claude/settings.json permissions.deny - which Cursor does not read, so this repository was protected on one host and not the other. failClosed, because a crashed guard must deny a read of a key file, not wave it through.

beforeTabFileRead.//: Tab reads files too, and a credential reaching the model through autocomplete is the same credential.

beforeSubmitPrompt.//: Advisory, and NOT failClosed on purpose: the reply shape for this event is {continue:boolean}, and a hook that crashes here would stop a person's message from being sent. Warning about a pasted credential is never worth deleting somebody's words.

sessionEnd.//: Writes the summary the next session on this worktree reads. Advisory and fail-open on purpose: a summary that could not be built is a lost convenience, and failing a person's session close over it would be the opposite mistake.

preCompact.//: The same script. Compaction is the moment the window is about to forget, so the record gets a marker rather than being replaced - the next reader can see the session continued past one.
